# SEO and GEO audit: acme-mugs The repo is a small client-side React and Vite app with 6 tracked files. Findings are ordered by severity. ## Critical **1. `public/robots.txt:1-2` blocks every crawler from the whole site.** `Disallow: /` under `User-agent: *` stops Google, Bing and all AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended and others). The site can't be indexed, cited or used in AI answers. Fix: ``` User-agent: * Allow: / Sitemap: https:///sitemap.xml ``` If you want to opt out of AI training but stay searchable, add per-bot `Disallow` blocks for specific bots only. If this file was meant to cover staging, serve it only there. **2. The site is client-side rendered only (`index.html:8`, `src/main.jsx:16`).** The served HTML is an empty `
`. Most AI crawlers don't run JavaScript, so they see no content. Googlebot does render JS, but later and less reliably. Fix: pre-render or server-render the routes. Options are SSG or prerender at build time (for example `vite-plugin-ssr`/Vike or `vite-react-ssg`), or moving to React Router framework mode or Next.js. At a minimum, prerender `/` and `/catalogue`. **3. Catalogue content loads after page load from `/api/mugs` (`src/pages/Catalogue.jsx:5-7`).** Products only appear after a client-side `fetch` in `useEffect`. Crawlers that don't run JS see only the `

`. Even the ones that do may not wait for the fetch to finish. Fix: fetch at build time or on the server and render the product list into the HTML. ## High **4. No page-level metadata (`index.html:4-6`).** - The title is the default `Vite App` (`index.html:5`). - There is no ``. - There is no ``. - There are no Open Graph or Twitter tags. - There is no `lang` attribute on `` (`index.html:2`) and no viewport meta tag (`index.html:4`). The viewport tag matters for mobile-first indexing. Fix: add `lang="en"` and a viewport tag. Give each route its own title, description and canonical, using React 19's native ``/`<meta>` hoisting or `react-helmet-async`. Put the `<title>`/`<meta>` tags in `Home.jsx` and `Catalogue.jsx`, or in a per-route head helper. **5. The catalogue has no per-product pages or links (`src/pages/Catalogue.jsx:11`).** Each mug is a bare `<p>` with only its name. There are no product URLs, so nothing can rank or be cited individually. There is also no price, description, image or availability. Fix: add a route like `/catalogue/:slug`, link to it with `<Link>`, and render name, description, price and image for each mug. **6. Navigation to the catalogue isn't crawlable (`src/main.jsx:11`).** The Catalogue entry is a `<button onClick={navigate(...)}>` rather than a link. Crawlers don't click buttons, so `/catalogue` is only discoverable through a sitemap, if you add one. Fix: `<Link to="/catalogue">Catalogue</Link>`. Also drop the now-unused `useNavigate` import (`src/main.jsx:2`). ## Medium **7. No structured data anywhere.** Add JSON-LD for the following: - `Organization` or `LocalBusiness` on Home. Mention Bristol and worldwide shipping. - `Product` with `Offer` (price, currency, availability) for each mug. - `BreadcrumbList` on product pages. Structured data helps rich results and gives AI engines unambiguous facts to quote. **8. No sitemap.** There is no `public/sitemap.xml` or generator, and `robots.txt` doesn't reference one. Generate it at build time from the routes and product list. **9. Image problems (`src/pages/Home.jsx:5`).** - `<img src="/hero.jpg" />` has no `alt`. Describe the image, for example `alt="Handmade ceramic mug on a wooden table"`. - There are no `width`/`height`, which causes layout shift (CLS). - If it's the hero or LCP image, add `fetchpriority="high"` and don't lazy-load it. Serve a modern format (WebP or AVIF) with `srcset`. **10. Thin content for GEO (`src/pages/Home.jsx:4-6`).** Home has one `<h1>` and one sentence. AI engines cite pages that answer questions directly. Add: - Short factual sections: materials, glaze, dishwasher and microwave safety, sizes, shipping times and costs, and returns. - An FAQ section, with `FAQPage` JSON-LD if you like. - About and contact content, to show who makes the mugs and their expertise. The catalogue page needs the same kind of descriptive text. ## Low **11. `src/pages/Catalogue.jsx:10` uses a generic `<h1>Catalogue</h1>`.** Use something descriptive, such as "Handmade ceramic mug catalogue". The same applies to the shared nav labels. **12. `<nav>` has no `aria-label` (`src/main.jsx:9`).** This is a small accessibility and semantics gain. **13. No `llms.txt` (optional).** Add `public/llms.txt` with a short site summary and links to key pages. Adoption by AI engines is inconsistent, so treat it as optional. **14. No fallback for loading or errors in `Catalogue.jsx:6`.** There is no `.catch` and no non-JS fallback. If the API fails, the page silently shows an empty catalogue. ## Suggested order 1. Fix `robots.txt` (#1). 2. Add prerendering or SSR (#2, #3). 3. Add per-route metadata (#4). 4. Add real `<Link>`s and product pages (#5, #6). 5. Add structured data, a sitemap, image fixes and richer content (#7–#10). I haven't changed any files. I can apply the quick fixes (#1, #4 for the static parts, #6, #9) now if you'd like. The prerendering choice in #2 is a bigger decision.
